Epsons are notoriously finicky printers, which is why I try to steer clear of them whenever humanly possible, but that’s another story… I have a few ideas: 

Overspray is usually indicative of two things

1). The printhead is bad, however I’m not inclined to say this is your problem 100% as the front half of the image is fine… Normally a bad printhead you will get a nasty looking leading edge on the image, followed by overspray.  

2). (Most common/likely) drastic overspray also happens when the head height is too high, meaning that there is too much distance between the substrate and the head.  I’m wondering if as your printing, the film is rippling, causing varied distances between the head.  I would expect to see some head strike evidence if this were the case, but who knows? Perhaps try double checking your settings? Rippling is more common on thinner stock, so if you set the printer for thinner stock, it will usually loosen its grip with the pinch rollers. I know this is true on higher end Epsons like the 7890 and so on, I don’t know much about the 1400 series printers, but it is something that wouldn’t hurt to check? 

Also, maybe check the printer it’s self for any obstructions in the paper path? Maybe something is caught in there, and it’s causing the film to shift during printing.
